payload.title: Repurposed antidepressants reduce MCF-7 viability at micromolar concentrations
payload.abstract: Several antidepressants have been reported to have antiproliferative activity, prompting repurposing interest in oncology. MCF-7 breast carcinoma cells were treated with sertraline, fluoxetine and paroxetine for 72 hours and viability was determined by sulforhodamine B staining. Sertraline gave an IC50 of 8.4 micromolar, fluoxetine 14.1 micromolar and paroxetine 22.6 micromolar. Apoptosis was confirmed by caspase 3 and 7 activation at the IC50 concentration for each compound. The cell model used throughout is mammary in origin, and no hepatic line or hepatocyte preparation was included in the study design.
